page: Microsoft Azure E16as_v6 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Eav6 server family. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz, configured with 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs via hyperthreading. The system features 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Text processing performance is highly competitive, ranking in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-core execution, database operations, and static web serving throughput fall within the average range. However, a notable performance tradeoff exists in memory subsystem behavior: while cached small-block read bandwidth is average, uncached large-block read bandwidth is weak, falling into the bottom 25%.

Given its high memory density of 8.0 GB per vCPU and dedicated CPU allocation, the E16as_v6 offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage. It is well-suited for relational databases, caching layers like Redis, enterprise applications, and memory-intensive data processing. It is less suitable for large-scale LLM inference or workloads constrained by uncached memory read speeds.
